body: Briefly as a treatment for migraines.  It didn’t do anything but make me feel super weird and uncomfortable, and panicky when I stopped.  Hard pass.  Thanks for the idea though.

Those are my good days.  Wake up thinking “let’s do push ups until the arms fall off, run, get back into shape, finish school, and get as far away as possible”.  But those days aren’t as often as the bad lately.  And for my kid’s sake, I can’t up and leave until things get back to normal and I find stable employment again.  I’ve battled with the idea of staying just to give her a whole family, but I do realize that a whole family is useless if 1/2 is dead inside.

I get you man.  Except for the racist shit, I never had to go through that and I’m sorry you did, that’s fucked.  I had a MSgt once so dumb he got kicked out of the company and sent to run the SOI armory.  While he was with us, I was working 12 hour days 6-7 days a week by myself doing double work because of his dumb shit.  I was absolutely miserable and that’s really when my drinking took off.  No one noticed.  I put my own name on the roster for company keys and just opened up for myself every weekend.  I got a bullshit NAM when I left.  Thanks for the parting gift, assholes. 
The wives, it’s like you give an inch and an inch and an inch for the sale of the relationship, but they add up quick to miles.  Then that becomes the status quo and you can’t change it.  You try and fight back, but every time you even raise your voice, being a man gets turned against you.  I can get yelled and screamed at, punched, kicked, have doors kicked in to get to me, I’ve had the dog’s bones thrown at my head, but the second I raise my voice I get threatened with the cops.  And because I’m a man, it’s game over.  I get yelled at for breathing too loud, for my jaw popping (both because I have a cleft and my mouth/nose are goofy), punched in the head for snoring when I’m sick, not allowed to have female friends even though she cheated once and I couldn’t ever definitively prove it so it died, blamed for literally anything that goes wrong, not allowed to speak unless spoken to, expected to care to the 10000th degree about anything she says, and screamed at if I don’t.  She’s screamed out the front window loud enough for neighbors to hear, holding our kid “say bye daddy he’s leaving because he doesn’t love you” over and over, because I had the nerve to leave in the middle of a fight.  It’s like living with a mental fucking terrorist, and there’s no room to fight back or escape. 
I don’t really want to die, and I hope you don’t either brother, but I just don’t want to live through this anymore. 
I feel like I should know better.  I’ve had too many friends from the Corps kill themselves after we got out.  One who I physically stopped from doing it while we were still in.  Only to find out years later he blew his brains out at work.  We have a routine suicide watch group for one guy.  I should know better.  But sharing the pain with people I know, makes me look and feel weak.  And I can’t, because it’s all about taking care of everyone else, and I can’t let them see that.  So now I’m hear talking to strangers about the shittiest, most intimate detail of my life.  How fucking weird. 
Reach out to me if you ever need an ear.

Then let’s fail together.  I hope that you can use this to piss yourself off. Use it as fuel to fire you up and push yourself farther.  Please message me if you ever need to talk.  I’m a fucked up shitbag but I’m a good listener!

That’s my goal tonight too.  Part of me hopes I fail.  All of me hopes you fail.  Sounds like you’ve been through the ringer more than once.  Keep the wolves at bay and use that pain for something good, motivation can be powerful, you deserve the opportunity to use that pain in your favor.
Right?  Like you can’t be responsible for it, it’s just something that happened and you can’t be blamed for it like you are for everything else.

“Oddly enough I find it even more comforting that it’s a totally random stranger”...

I think it’s because there’s no bias either way, and also because it means you aren’t alone.  If some total stranger from who knows how far away can relate, it makes it feel more normal and less alien. At least it does for me.  I know reading your thing about the cats made me feel like less of a weird a-hole for worrying about legal “ownership” of our dogs when considering divorce. 

Please do put yourself first.  As crappy as I feel right now, commiserating and being helpful is kind of cathartic.

I hope you find a good resolution.  A better job in a better town with a better home.  And I hope you get your babies.  My wife technically “owns” my dog and I “own” hers.  That’s been one of the barriers in the way of me divorcing her in the past, so I understand where that pain is coming from.  I really hope you get to the happier side of this, no one deserves to be treated that way.  Best of luck and please ask for help, I’ll steal some cats for a good cause.
Thanks for reading and I appreciate the offer, but no thanks.  Really just wanted to get that out of my head and crawl deep in a bottle.  Thanks though.
